system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — HCBF Holding Company, Inc. / Harbor Community Bank realized record after combination with CenterState Bank Corporation, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the acquired entity deregistered from SEC
> reporting shortly after closing and its acquirer itself later deregistered following a
> further transaction, no periodic report by any entity in the chain is available to
> trace the acquired business's own trajectory within the fixed outcome window. This
> sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured at
> closing.

## Public-reporting status of the acquired entity after the transaction
- HCBF Holding Company, Inc. filed a Form 15-15D on 2018-01-11 (shortly after the merger
  became effective on January 1, 2018), certifying termination/suspension of its duty to
  file periodic reports under Sections 13 and 15(d) of the Exchange Act. No further
  periodic reports (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K) by HCBF appear in EDGAR after this filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-18-001805, Form 15-15D]
- At the effective time of the merger, HCBF's directors and executive officers ceased
  serving in those capacities; HCBF ceased to exist as a separate legal entity, merged
  into CenterState. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-18-000005, Form 8-K (HCBF), Items 2.01/5.02]

## Public-reporting status of the direct acquirer within the outcome window
- CenterState Bank Corporation (the direct acquirer of HCBF, CIK 0001102266), continued
  to file its own periodic reports for roughly two years after the HCBF merger, with its
  last annual report on Form 10-K covering fiscal year 2019, filed 2020-02-27. [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-20-007443, Form 10-K FY2019]
- On June 7, 2020, CenterState itself completed a "merger of equals" with South State
  Corporation, with South State as the surviving public company; at the effective time
  CenterState's own directors and executive officers ceased serving in those
  capacities. CenterState subsequently filed a Form 25-NSE (2020-06-08) and a Form
  15-12G (2020-06-18) terminating its own Exchange Act registration. [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-20-028550, Form 8-K (CenterState), completion of merger of equals]; [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-171864, Form 15-12G]
- Consequently, within the fixed ~2020-2022 outcome window (approximately 3-5 years
  after the HCBF combination closed on January 1, 2018), neither HCBF nor its direct
  acquirer CenterState remained a distinct SEC-reporting entity; any subsequent
  consolidated reporting is that of South State Corporation (later SouthState Bank
  Corp, CIK 0000764038), a company formed through a further, separate combination. [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-20-028550, Form 8-K (CenterState)]

## Search for a separately disclosed business record
- A full-text search of SEC EDGAR filings dated 2020-01-01 through 2023-12-31 for the
  phrase "Harbor Community Bank" returns no hits among any registrant's Form 10-K
  filings. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/#/q=%22Harbor%20Community%20Bank%22&forms=10-K&dateRange=custom&startdt=2020-01-01&enddt=2023-12-31 (EDGAR full-text search, 0 results)]
- A full-text search for "HCBF" across all SEC filings dated 2021-01-01 through
  2023-12-31 returns 8 results, none of which are filings by CenterState Bank Corp,
  South State Corporation/SouthState Bank Corp, or any other successor entity
  referencing HCBF Holding Company or its former business (the matches are unrelated
  registrants, e.g. Herzfeld Caribbean Basin Fund, Harbor Funds, First Foundation Inc.). [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/#/q=%22HCBF%22&dateRange=custom&startdt=2021-01-01&enddt=2023-12-31 (EDGAR full-text search, 8 results, none related to HCBF Holding Company)]
- No reputable-press article documenting a distinct post-2018 operating or financial
  trajectory for the former HCBF/Harbor Community Bank business (as opposed to the
  combined CenterState or South State enterprise) was located. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- No periodic SEC filing traces a separate 3-5-year realized record for the acquired
  business: HCBF deregistered within two weeks of closing, and the direct acquirer
  (CenterState) itself ceased to be an independent SEC registrant approximately 2.5
  years after the HCBF combination, having been absorbed in turn into South State
  Corporation. No entity in this chain discloses HCBF/Harbor Community Bank's trajectory
  as a distinct line item in the fixed outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-18-001805, Form 15-15D]; [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-171864, Form 15-12G]

[SLICE END]
